subject: Dedicated reservation: commit curve, burst runbook, and activation options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@tesseract.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation: commit curve, burst runbook, and activation options

Samir —

Thanks for the good discussion this morning. Per our call, attached is an options-level proposal that ties cluster sizing and ramp cadence to expected Q4 product launches at Tesseract. I sketched three approaches so your architecture and procurement teams can compare economics vs. operational flexibility. High level: we keep the same model catalog and runtime guarantees; the difference is how you commit to minimum GPUs and how we provision burst capacity during peak launches.

Summary (attachments: tesseract_dedicated_offer_v1.pdf, commit-curve-pricing-sheet.xlsx):

1) Flex Curve (recommended for unpredictable launch cadence)
- Minimum committed baseline: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (24/7).
- Planned ramp: Week 0: 16 -> Week 4: 32 -> Month 3: 48 -> Month 6: 64 (ramp checkpoints tied to usage milestones).
- Early-burst runway: +30% burst pool available for first 90 days (consumed as burst credits, metered).
- SLA: 99.9% availability on committed baseline; best-effort for burst above baseline.

2) Anchored Floor (predictable throughput, lower per-unit price)
- Minimum committed baseline: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Flat monthly profile (no scheduled ramp).
- Includes reserved warm cache and pre-loaded model slices for pinned versions.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime on baseline; prioritized scheduling for background batch jobs.

3) Staircase Commit (step commitments aligned to product milestones)
- Minimum committed baseline: 12 GPUs initial, auto-increase to 24 at Month 2, 48 at Month 5.
- Includes two free 48-hour surge windows per quarter to cover launch spikes.
- Ideal if procurement wants smaller initial spend but deterministic future commits.

Operational notes and differentiators:
- Cross-region bursting: available but billed as egress + cross-region capacity hours; helpful for geo failover.
- Warmup credits: we include an activation buffer (GPU-hours) so you avoid cold-cache tail latency during first 72 hours after a ramp step.
- Model pinning: you can pin a specific model variant and we prioritize kernels and KV cache slots for it; rollback path included.

Request: can you confirm which of the three you'd prefer for procurement to evaluate? If helpful, I can turn this into a mutual action plan with milestones and signatures. Also looping in Karthik to confirm the discount curve for deal sizing and Monica to outline onboarding timeline.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0133

Vivek —

Thanks for sending. Quick questions from our side before we loop procurement in for formal review: 

1) For the Flex Curve, how do you price the early-burst runway? Is it a blended per-GPU-hour rate or a premium on top of on-demand?
2) For cross-region bursts (we're considering EU failover), can you guarantee KV cache warmup time or is that best-effort?
3) If we choose Staircase Commit, are the surge windows transferrable between quarters? Our launches can shift.

Also can you confirm whether the Anchored Floor option supports separate queues for real-time vs. batch (we need stricter latency for inference).

If you can get Karthik's numbers for per-GPU effective price at 12/24/48/64 commitments that will help procurement move quickly.

Best,
Samir Rao
VP Engineering — Tesseract AI
samir@tesseract.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@tesseract.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, procurement@tesseract.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation: commit curve, burst runbook, and activation options

Samir —

Answers inline below, and Karthik added pricing bullets after.

1) Flex Curve burst pricing: burst runway is invoiced as GPU-hour consumption at on-demand rate but we apply a 15% blended discount on burst hours for the first 90 days (this is the "early-burst credit"). After day 90 burst hours revert to standard on-demand pricing. We also provide a monthly burst cap configurable by you to prevent runaway spend.

2) Cross-region KV warmup: KV cache warmup is best-effort across regions. We guarantee a 95th percentile warmup time SLA for same-region ramps (i.e., warming pre-cached keys within 30 minutes for typical traffic patterns). For cross-region failover we recommend a pre-warmed cold-standby (small committed baseline in EU) or using our synchronous replication add-on (details in the attachment).

3) Staircase surge windows: surge windows are transferable between adjacent quarters up to two transfers per year; unused surge windows expire after 12 months. We can include roll-over terms in the MSA if needed.

Anchored Floor: yes — we support queue separation (hard partitioning) for real-time inference lanes vs. batch lanes. That is part of the Anchored Floor SKU and is enforced by placement policies; real-time lanes get pre-allocated inference slots and lower latency scheduling.

Pricing (Karthik):
- 12 GPU baseline: $38.50 / GPU-hour effective (list: $48.00)
- 24 GPU baseline: $34.00 / GPU-hour effective
- 48 GPU baseline: $28.75 / GPU-hour effective
- 64+ GPU baseline: $24.90 / GPU-hour effective
Discount notes: the Staircase Commit gets an enrollment discount applied at the time of each step; Flex Curve includes a small operational premium but more burst flexibility.

Karthik — can you confirm these numbers on the sheet so procurement has a single row view?

Monica — can you draft a 6-week onboarding timeline for the Flex Curve option (if they pick it) that includes model pinning, KV cache sizing, and travis-style smoke tests?

Thanks,
Vivek

Per Karthik and Monica's updates, attached is a clean offer reflecting the Staircase Commit variant (we put in explicit surge-window transfer terms and added the early-burst credit language). If procurement is happy with the legal language we can route to DocuSign (link included).

Key execution items before signature:
- Finalize baseline sizing (we penciled 12 -> 24 -> 48 over 5 months).
- Confirm per-quarter surge window allotment and any transfer rules you need changed.
- Provide list of pinned model variants and any compliance evidence (SOC2 report) you require; we attached SOC2 reference link in the DocuSign envelope.

Next steps: I can send a mutual action plan with milestones and dates once you confirm baseline sizing. If you'd like, we can provision the initial 12-GPU baseline in a staging pool and run the 72-hour warmup/validation before signature (this reduces first-week risk).

Thanks,
Vivek
